problem: The priority-dev interpreter improves only on recorded transcripts. The optimiser runs on old sessions no longer give useful feedback. The engineer does not remember those sessions well enough to judge a reading.
why_now: D1 beats the base prompt by 0.185 on 56 test stops, and D2 does not beat D1. The next gain needs a different signal: readings of sessions that the engineer remembers.
approach: An opt-in plugin, cobuilder-priority, ships one hooks module. A per-session switch is off by default. With the switch on, a Stop hook on the main loop runs priority digest, then priority interpret with the D1 program, as a separate process, and returns at once. The module stores each reading. A pane shows one card per stop, with right, wrong, and note marks. On the newest card, the person selects steps, and one press sends the draft to the session or puts it in the prompt box.

alternatives.option: A Stop command hook with async true, plus a mod pane that reads its files
alternatives.rejected_because: Two mechanisms meet through a data folder. One hooks module can start the process and draw the pane, so no file hand-off is necessary.

alternatives.option: Interpret only, one model call per stop
alternatives.rejected_because: The engineer wants the digest of the run in the brief. The brief labels it CURRENT RUN on the live path.
Interpret would read the digest of the stop before, not of this stop. The engineer chose digest first.

alternatives.option: Change the PREVIOUS RUN label in every command
alternatives.rejected_because: Eval, replay, and the optimiser would see a new brief, and earlier compact-brief scores would no longer compare.

alternatives.option: Read every session in every repo
alternatives.rejected_because: Each transcript goes to an outside model service. The engineer chose a per-session switch that is off by default.
The engineer chose a per-session switch, so each read is a choice made in that session.

alternatives.option: Ship the D1 program inside the plugin
alternatives.rejected_because: priority-dev/probes/programs/ is Git-ignored. The person names the program file in userConfig.
The priority-dev CLI already reads priority-dev/.env. A secret userConfig key is an optional override.

alternatives.option: Show the steps and carry out none
alternatives.rejected_because: The engineer wants to act on a reading, and a sent step is a stronger label than a mark.

alternatives.option: Carry out the selected steps with no press
alternatives.rejected_because: Model text from the transcript reaches the session only after the person reads it and presses Send or Edit.

alternatives.option: Write each mark into the confirmed label files
alternatives.rejected_because: The engineer keeps the labels local. Live marks are a separate record from the confirmed set.
Each turn costs two model calls on an outside service. A person must choose that.

alternatives.option: A Claude Artifact page instead of a pane
alternatives.rejected_because: A page does not sit beside the session and update at each stop.

out_of_scope: A step sent with no press, and a send from an older card
An interrupt step, which has no running turn to stop at a stop
An operating-system notice for a notify step
An export of the marks into the labelled set
An optimiser run on the marks
Subagent stops, headless sessions, and other harnesses
A change to D1, to eval, to replay, or to the optimiser
risks: D1 was not scored on a brief with a CURRENT RUN digest, so its readings can be worse than 0.654.
Each stop with the switch on costs two model calls on an outside service.
A hot reload or the end of the session can stop a reading, and that stop gets no card.
The transcript can lag behind the Stop event, so the brief can miss the last reply.
A model wrote the draft from the transcript. A careless press can send text that the person did not read.
testing: claude plugin test drives the module through classic.Stop, command.run, and ui.render, with a stubbed $.process.run. pytest covers the --digest current flag in priority-dev.
reviewer_focus: The install-surface amendment to ADR-0025 and ADR-0039
The run guard: one reading at a time, and only the newest waiting stop
The CURRENT RUN label: live path only
The send guard: a press, the visible draft, and the newest card only
unknowns: Does a reading that the hook does not await survive until its process ends?
How long does the transcript lag behind the Stop event? This is question 3 of adapter-host.md section 7.
How long do the digest and interpret calls take on a live stop?
Does a terminal pane scroll when the cards are taller than the pane? The layout closes older cards, so it does not depend on it.
